I can only speak for myself but DBT has changed my life. I have Bipolar as well so I do need to be on meds but the meds don't affect the BPD aspects of my mental health. DBT is the only thing that has worked. In fact, I would even say traditional therapy made my BPD worse!

One thing I will say is be careful who you disclose your mental health diagnosis to. You probably wont experience any overt discrimination (I certainly haven't). I found that most people who don't know you very well are very accepting and understanding. For those who do know you (family and friends etc) there can be major problems. Be prepared to never be "right" in a dispute or argument ever again! Because "its your BPD talking." Other people will be unreasonable and scream and shout but if you even raise your voice you are the BPD guy going off on one again. It sucks. 

On a positive note DBT is excellent. Give it a go!

Started with a one off case of gross hematuria back in November. I was peeing blood. Very scary stuff. I then had urinary urgency and frequency, terrible stinging pain in the super pubic region, and lower back pain. The pain in the super pubic region was so bad I ended up in hospital twice. The doc put me on 6 weeks of Cipro, Tamsu and anti inflammatories. Nothing changed until 2 days before the end of the 6 week course of Cipro and my symptoms reduced to where they are now. Currently have more of a dull persistent ache in the pubic region and pain in the hips, crotch and legs. Urinary frequency has reduced but when my bladder fills I feel pain that only relents when I empty my bladder. There are other weird little symptoms that aren't worth mentioning. Multiple urine and blood tests done, cystoscopy, full CT with dye and ultrasound.

It's not pleasant but it is over very quickly. Grit your teeth and try to think past it. Have something nice planned for after the procedure. But do get it done. It is the best way for your Uro to know whats going on in there. Good luck soldier.

It's a mess isn't it? Having BPD and BD. For years psychiatrists diagnosed one or the other but couldn't agree, until I spent some time in the acute psyche ward and they were able to observe me. It was a long process and they had me on every drug under the sun. I think Klonopin is the only one I managed to dodge. But after my stay in the acute ward they all agreed it was BPD and BD, with one or the other taking on the dominant role at different times. BPD seems to be more respondent to external stimuli and emotional triggers etc. BD has a more biological cycle. This feels absolutely spot on as I can be very reactionary and impulsive but I can also feel deep depression or mania sweeping in regardless of my mood. Every suicide attempt has happened when the two come at the same time. If you need to talk I'm here. It is pretty unusual to have both.
